subject: Post-call recap: BlueCedar pilot affordability & token-econ levers
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@bluecedar.com>, Rahul Sen <rahul.sen@bluecedar.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: BlueCedar pilot affordability & token-econ levers

Hi Asha / Rahul — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything on the same page.

What we heard (primary pains):
- Customer-facing fraud scoring is adding manual review overhead and slowdowns at peak (up to 40% increase in handling time).
- Latency spikes at 95/99p are impacting conversion; target is 95p < 150ms for scoring calls.
- Token spend is unpredictable across user flows; procurement has a hard pilot budget (~$25–30k/mo).

Goals you stated:
- Prove we can drop manual review volume by 20–30% via improved scoring quality and latency.
- Run a scoped pilot that fits within procurement constraints and gives a clear unit-econ signal (cost per prevented fraud case).
- Confirm security/compliance fit (SOC2 + network controls) before production.

Key levers we discussed (impact/notes):
- Batching: combine low-latency, near-real-time requests into micro-batches for back-end enrichment to reduce per-token overhead (expected 20–40% token savings in high-throughput windows).
- KV/prefix caching: cache user session context for repeat interactions to avoid re-sending long prompts (best for returning users; up to ~50% token reduction on repeated flows).
- Model variant + quantization: trade off small quality delta for 3–4x cheaper token cost on lower-tier variants for non-critical scoring tiers.

Initial TCO scenarios (very high level; detailed workbook attached):
1) Narrow pilot — 6 weeks, high-risk transactions only (est. 100k tokens/day) — projected hosted spend + Redwood savings tooling: ~$18–24k/mo equivalent run-rate.
2) Scoped pilot — 6 weeks, mixed risk (est. 200k tokens/day + caching) — projected spend: ~$28–33k/mo; expected net cost after batching savings: ~30–35% lower than naive run.
3) Expanded test — sustained, production-like (500k tokens/day) — requires reserved/dedicated pricing conversation; sizable savings possible but needs committed capacity.

Attachments I left: Redwood_TCO_v1.xlsx (breakdowns by batch factor / cache hit / model variant), SOW_BlueCedar_template.pdf (pilot ops + deliverables).

Immediate next steps
- Redwood: update the TCO workbook with BlueCedar traffic profile and a recommended 6-week pilot scope & SOW by COB Aug 25.
- BlueCedar: share a sample traffic distribution (CSV with request rates by hour and typical prompt length) + procurement constraints / approval timeline. (Asha — can procurement circulate timeline?)
- Security: we flagged SOC2 docs; I'll send the compliance packet after we lock scope.

If the $25k/month hard cap is real, we should scope to the Narrow or Scoped pilot above and trade off coverage vs. depth of evaluation. Happy to walk through the workbook together.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Vanessa — thanks for the thorough summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement has communicated a firm pilot budget of ~$25k/month (hard gate). We can stretch at most by re-allocating a small PoC fund, but not beyond that without exec approval.
- Our current priority is reducing manual review overhead. If the pilot proves quality improvements for high-risk transactions, we can expand later.

I've attached a sample traffic export (BlueCedar_sample_traffic.csv) that shows hourly volumes and median prompt lengths for the last 90 days. It skews heavy in the evening peak window (18:00–22:00 EST).

Would it be possible to run the Narrow pilot (100k tokens/day) focused only on the top 2 fraud workflows and show a phased path to the 200k/day scope if we hit the 20% manual review reduction metric?

Asha Patel
Head of Risk Operations, BlueCedar Financial
asha@bluecedar.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BlueCedar pilot affordability & token-econ levers

Asha — great, appreciate the sample export and the budget clarity. Based on the CSV you shared and the $25k pilot cap, here's a concrete proposal that fits procurement while giving a clear eval: 

Proposed pilot (fits $25k cap)
- Duration: 6 weeks (4 weeks run + 1 week ramp + 1 week analysis).
- Scope: Top 2 fraud/workflow endpoints only (approx. 40% of fraud volume according to your file).
- Sizing: target ~150k tokens/day average (centered on peak windows) — this gives headroom beyond the 100k narrow ask but remains under your spend cap when batching & caching are applied.
- Expected economics: with modest batching (1.5–2.0x effective batching on back-end flows) and KV caching on repeat sessions, we estimate a 30–35% net token cost reduction vs baseline. That should give a defensible ROI within the pilot window assuming a 20% reduction in manual review.

Deliverables at pilot end
- Unit-econ dashboard (token cost, latency percentiles, manual review reduction estimates).
- Short-runbook for production rollout (batching knobs, cache TTLs, fallback model mapping).
- Recommended model variant + quantization profile for each scoring tier.

Next operational steps
1) I will update Redwood_TCO_v1.xlsx with the traffic CSV assumptions and a cost sheet tuned to the 150k/day pilot by EOD Aug 24.
2) I'll send an editable SOW (SOW_BlueCedar_template.pdf) with pilot milestones; please ask procurement to return a signed SOW or redlines by Aug 30 so legal can route.
3) Security team will queue SOC2 artifacts once scope is locked — I'll share the packet in parallel.

If procurement needs a clean line item that isolates risk (e.g., credit holdback for quality metrics), we can propose an SLA-based refund/rollover. Happy to detail that in the SOW.

Best —
Vanessa

Subject: Internal: BlueCedar negotiation posture and pricing ask

Marissa / Aditya — quick internal note following Asha's reply. Procurement is firm at $25k/mo for pilot. They are willing to take a slightly bigger scope if we can show a >30% token-cost reduction via batching + caching — that becomes our negotiation lever.

Recommended playbook:
- Offer the 6-week, 150k/day pilot as discussed but prepare a pricing exception template that reduces our hosted list price by ~12–18% conditioned on batching/caching metrics hitting targets. This will keep the deal economical for them and protects our margin if they don’t hit batch factors.
- Marissa: can you draft the pricing exception (line items + SLA refund clause) so I can attach to the SOW?
- Aditya: please pre-run the 150k/day cost scenario in the TCO workbook with batch factors 1.3 / 1.6 / 2.0 and a conservative cache hit of 25% — we want three lines to show to procurement.

I'll own SOW edits and the kickoff calendar. If procurement pushes for lower cost, we can offer a shorter ramp (3 weeks) with the option to expand.

Thanks —
Vanessa
